_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: नन्वीश्वरस्य तव जन्मादिशून्यत्वं सत्यमेव जीवानां तु जन्ममरणे प्रसिद्धे तत्राह देहिन इति
objection: it is indeed true that You, the Lord, are free from birth and the rest, but birth and death of individual souls are well known; to this he says ‘of the embodied’
देहिनो देहाभिमानिनो जीवस्य यथाऽस्मिन्स्थूलदेहे कौमाराद्यवस्था देहनिबन्धना एव नतु स्वतः
for the embodied individual soul, one identifying with the body, stages such as childhood in this gross body depend on the body alone, not on the Self itself
पूर्वावस्थानाशेऽवस्थान्तरोत्पत्तावपि स एवाहमिति प्रत्यभिज्ञानात्
because even when a previous state is destroyed and another state arises, there is recognition ‘I am that very same one’
तथैवैतद्देहनाशे देहान्तरप्राप्तिरपि लिङ्गदेहनिबन्धना
likewise, when this body is destroyed, attainment of another body also depends on the subtle body
नतु तावतात्मनो नाशः
but there is no destruction of the Self
जातमात्रस्य पूर्वसंस्कारेण स्तन्यपानादौ प्रवृत्तिदर्शनात्
because a newly born child is seen to engage in sucking milk and the like through previous impressions
अतो धीरः धीमांस्तत्र तयोर्देहनाशोत्पत्त्योर्न मुह्यति आत्मैव मृतो जातश्चेति न मन्यते
therefore the steady, intelligent person is not deluded by the destruction and arising of bodies and does not think that the Self itself has died or been born
ननु गतानागतानहं न शोचामि किंतु तद्वियोगादिदुःखभाजमात्मानमेवेति चेत्तत्राह मात्रास्पर्शा इति
objection: I do not grieve for the dead or living; rather I grieve for myself as one suffering from separation from them and so forth; to this he says ‘contacts of the senses’
मीयन्ते ज्ञायन्ते विषया आभिरिति मात्रा इन्द्रियवृत्तयः
‘mātrāḥ’ are functions of the senses, by which objects are measured, known
तासां स्पर्शाः विषयैः संबन्धाः ते शीतोष्णादिप्रदा भवन्ति
their contacts, connections with objects, produce cold, heat, and the like
ते त्वागमापायित्वादनित्या अस्थिराः अतस्तांस्तितिक्षस्व सहस्व
because they come and go, they are impermanent, unstable; therefore endure them, bear them
यथा जलातपादिसंपर्कास्तत्तत्कालकृताः स्वभावतः शीतोष्णादि प्रयच्छन्ति
just as contacts with water, sunlight, and the like, occurring at their respective times, naturally produce cold, heat, and the like
एवमिष्टसंयोगवियोगा अपि सुखदुःखादि प्रयच्छन्ति
so also union with and separation from desired objects produce pleasure, pain, and the like
तेषां चास्थिरत्वात्सहनं तव धीरस्योचितं नतु तन्निमित्तहर्षविषादपारवश्यमित्यर्थः
because they are unstable, endurance is proper for a steady person like you, not subjection to joy and grief caused by them; this is the meaning
तत्प्रतीकारप्रयत्नादपि तत्सहनमेवोचितं महाफलत्वादित्याह यमिति
rather than striving to counteract them, endurance alone is proper because it bears a great fruit; he says this with ‘whom’
एते मात्रास्पर्शाः यं पुरुषं न व्यथयन्ति नाभिभवन्ति
the person whom these sense-contacts do not afflict or overpower
समे सुख दुःखे यस्य तम्
one for whom pleasure and pain are equal
स तैरविक्षिप्यमाणो धर्मज्ञानद्वारा अमृतत्वाय मोक्षाय कल्पते योग्यो भवति
not being disturbed by them, he becomes fit for immortality, liberation, through dharma and knowledge
ननु तथापि शीतोष्णादिकमतिदुःसहं कथं सोढव्यम् अत्यन्तं तत्सहने च कदाचिद्देहनाशस्यापि संभवादित्याशङ्क्य
objection: nevertheless, how can cold, heat, and the like, which are exceedingly hard to bear, be endured? by enduring them excessively there may even be destruction of the body
तत्त्वविचारतः सर्वं सोढुं शक्यमित्याशयेनाह नेति
anticipating this, with the intention that everything can be endured through inquiry into reality, he says ‘not’
असतः अनात्मधर्मत्वादविद्यमानस्य शीतोष्णादेरात्मनि भावः सत्ता न विद्यते
the unreal, cold and heat and the like, being attributes of the non-Self and therefore not truly existing, have no being, no existence, in the Self
तथा सतः सत्स्वभावस्यात्मनोऽभावो विनाशो न विद्यते
likewise, for the real, the Self whose nature is being, there is no non-being, no destruction
एवमुभयोः सदसतोरन्तो निर्णयो दृष्टः
thus the final determination regarding both the real and unreal has been seen
कैः तत्त्वदर्शिभिर्वस्तुयाथात्म्यविद्भिः
by whom? by seers of truth, knowers of things as they really are
एवंभूतविवेकेन सहस्वेत्यर्थः
endure through discrimination of this kind; this is the meaning
तत्र सत्स्वभावमविनाशि वस्तु सामान्येनोक्तं विशेषतो दर्शयति अविनाशीति
the indestructible reality of the nature of being was stated generally; he shows it specifically with ‘indestructible’
येन सर्वमिदमागमापायधर्मकं देहादि ततं तत्साक्षित्वेन व्याप्तम्
that by which all this, beginning with the body and characterized by coming and going, is pervaded as its witness
तत्तु आत्मस्वरूपमविनाशि विनाशशून्यं विद्धि जानीहि
know that, the nature of the Self, to be indestructible, devoid of destruction
तत्र हेतुमाह विनाशमिति
he states the reason for this with ‘destruction’
आगमापायधर्मकं संदर्शयति अन्तवन्त इति
he shows what is characterized by coming and going with ‘having an end’
अन्तो विनाशो विद्यते येषां तेऽन्तवन्तः
those in which an end, destruction, exists are ‘having an end’
नित्यस्य सर्वदैकरुपस्य शरीरिणः शरीरवतः अतएव अनाशिनो विनाशरहितस्य अप्रमेयस्य अपरिच्छिन्नस्य आत्मन इमे सुखदुःखादिधर्मका देहा उक्तास्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः

these bodies, characterized by pleasure, pain, and the like, are declared by seers of truth to belong to the eternal embodied Self, always of one form, and therefore indestructible, without destruction, immeasurable, unlimited
यस्मादेवमात्मनो न विनाशः नच सुखदुःखादिसंबन्धः तस्मान्मोहजं शोकं त्यक्त्वा युध्यस्व
because the Self is thus not destroyed and has no connection with pleasure, pain, and the like, abandon grief born of delusion and fight
स्वधर्मे मा त्याक्षीरित्यर्थः
do not abandon your own dharma; this is the meaning
तदेवं भीष्मादिमृत्युनिमित्तः शोको निवारितः
thus grief caused by the death of Bhīṣma and the others has been removed
यच्चात्मनो हन्तृत्वनिमित्तं दुःखमुक्तं एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि इत्यादिना तदपि तद्वदेव निर्निमित्तमित्याह य एनमिति
and the distress stated on account of the Self’s being a killer, in ‘I do not wish to kill these’ and so forth, is equally without cause; he says this with ‘he who this’
एनमात्मानम्
‘this’ means this Self
आत्मनो हननक्रियायां कर्मत्वं कर्तृत्वमपि नास्तीत्यर्थः
the Self is neither object nor agent in the act of killing; this is the meaning
तत्र हेतुर्नायमिति
he gives the reason with ‘this is not’
न हन्यत इत्येतदेव षड्भावविकारशून्यत्वेन द्रढयति नेति
he confirms ‘it is not killed’ by showing that it is free from the six transformations of being, with ‘not’
न जायत इति जन्मप्रतिषेधः
‘it is not born’ denies birth
न म्रियते चेति विनाशप्रतिषेधः
‘nor does it die’ denies destruction
वाशब्दौ चार्थे
the two occurrences of ‘vā’ have the sense of ‘and’
नचायं भूत्वा उत्पद्य भविता भवति अस्तित्वं भजते
nor, having come to be, having arisen, does it afterwards become existent
किंतु प्रागेव स्वतः सद्रूप इति जन्मानन्तरास्तित्वलक्षणद्वितीयविकारप्रतिषेधः
rather, it is by its own nature already existent; thus the second transformation, existence after birth, is denied
तत्र हेतुः यस्मादजः
the reason is: because it is unborn
यो हि जायते स जन्मानन्तरमस्तित्वं भजते नतु यः स्वयमेवास्ति स भूयोऽप्यन्यदस्तित्वं भजत इत्यर्थः
what is born acquires existence after birth; but what exists by itself does not acquire some further existence; this is the meaning
नित्यः सर्वदैकरुप इति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधः
‘eternal, always of one form’ denies growth
शाश्वतः शश्वद्भव इत्यपक्षयप्रतिषेधः
‘everlasting, always existing’ denies decline
पुराण इति विपरिणामप्रतिषेधः
‘ancient’ denies transformation
पुरापि नव एव नतु परिणामतो रुपान्तरं प्राप्य नवो भवतीत्यर्थः
even formerly it is ever fresh; it does not become new by changing and taking another form; this is the meaning
यद्वा न भवितेत्यस्यानुषङ्गं कृत्वा भूयोऽधिकं यथा भवति तथा न भवतीति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधः
or, carrying forward ‘will not become,’ it does not become more than it was; thus growth is denied
अजो नित्य इति चोभयवृद्ध्यभावे हेतुरित्यपौनरुक्त्यम्
‘unborn’ and ‘eternal’ are reasons for the absence of both kinds of growth, so there is no redundancy
तदेवं जायते अस्ति वर्धते विपरिणमते अपक्षीयते नश्यतीत्येवं यास्कादिभिर्वेदवादिभिरुक्ताः षड्भावविकारा निरस्ताः
thus the six transformations stated by Yāska and other Vedic authorities—birth, existence, growth, transformation, decline, and destruction—are denied
यदर्थमेते विकारा निरस्तास्तं प्रस्तुतं विनाशाभावमुपसंहरति न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीर इति
he concludes the intended absence of destruction, for whose sake these transformations were denied: ‘it is not killed when the body is killed’
अतएव हन्तृत्वाभावोऽपि पूर्वोक्तः प्रसिद्ध इत्याह वेदेति
therefore the previously stated absence of agency in killing is also established; he says this with ‘knows’
नित्यं वृद्धिशून्यम् अव्ययमपक्षयशून्यम् अजमविनाशिनं च यो वेद
one who knows it as eternal, free from growth; undecaying, free from decline; unborn and indestructible
स पुरुषः कं हन्ति कथं वा हन्ति
whom does that person kill, or how does he kill?
एवंभूतस्य वधे साधनाभावात्
because there is no means for killing such a Self
तथा स्वयं प्रयोजको भूत्वाऽन्येन कं घातयति
likewise, becoming the instigator himself, whom does he cause another to kill?
न कंचिदपि कथंचिदपीत्यर्थः
no one at all, in any way; this is the meaning
अनेन मय्यपि प्रयोजकत्वाद्दोषदृष्टिं मा कार्षीरित्युक्तं भवति
by this it is also said: do not see fault in Me on the ground that I am the instigator
नन्वात्मनोऽविनाशित्वेऽपि तदीयशरीरनाशं पर्यालोच्य शोचामीति चेत्तत्राह वासांसीति
objection: even if the Self is indestructible, I grieve considering the destruction of its body; to this he says ‘garments’
कर्मनिबन्धनभूतानां देहानामवश्यंभावित्वान्न जीर्णदेहनाशे शोकावकाश इत्यर्थः
because bodies, which are bound by karma, necessarily arise, there is no occasion for grief over the destruction of an old body; this is the meaning
